solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old college degrees dons change

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so one word is worn around the other here

parts.note: to change is to alter
two MAs, Master of Arts degrees, plural

explanation.surface: Dons at a university keep altering the degrees on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like the college teachers, but it is the verb: ALTER puts on MA MA like a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduate's former university or school is affectionately called by this Latin phrase meaning nourishing mother.

clue.text: Means of taking soundings when detectives turned up

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives arrive just as depths are being sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: An early sonar system used to detect submarines by echoes.

clue.text: Embassy official, one with torn tatty camelhair jacket

indicators.note: jacket means to wrap round, so the scrambled letters enclose the numeral
torn means ripped apart, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A diplomat wears a ripped, shabby camelhair jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' scrambles TATTY CAMELHAIR, and 'jacket' wraps those letters round I.
explanation.definitionFit: An army officer posted to a foreign embassy to advise on defence.

clue.text: Pirate gold confiscated by organised armed resistance

indicators.note: confiscated by means taken into, so the metal goes inside
organised means arranged, so the letters of armed are rearranged

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Pirate treasure is seized by an armed resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' turns ARMED into MARDE; add R, and 'confiscated by' puts AU inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider who roams in search of plunder.

clue.text: Solicitor back in court over case from Utrecht

indicators.note: back in picks the final letter of the word court

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: case from takes the outer shell of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A lawyer returns to court to deal with a case from the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: A solicitor in the sense of one who solicits custom: a ticket tout.
explanation.definitionFit: A tout is someone who pesters people for business, touting or soliciting.

clue.text: Famous conductor Last's last hip-hop banger

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor

indicators.note: the second last picks the closing letter of the name before it

parts.note: rap is hip-hop music

explanation.surface: Bandleader James Last's final album turns out to be a hip-hop banger.
explanation.walkthrough: James Last was a bandleader, so 'Famous conductor Last' reads as one person; it is RATTLE then the last letter of Last. A banger is British slang for an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is British slang for a battered old car, a noisy wreck.

clue.text: Allegorical painter spouted nonsense

indicators.note: spouted means spoken out at length, so the word for nonsense is heard rather than written

parts.note: bosh is a dated word for nonsense

explanation.surface: An allegorical painter is accused of talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Hieronymus Bosch, the Dutch painter of The Garden of Earthly Delights.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch painted moralising allegories crowded with symbolic figures.

clue.text: Military badge always pinned up by baronet

indicators.note: pinned by means fixed inside, so the reversed word sits within the abbreviation
in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A baronet always has a military badge pinned to his chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EVER into REVE, and 'pinned' puts it inside BT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviators' wings are this kind of insignia, worn on a uniform.

clue.text: One helping you mind your p's and q's?

definitions.text: One helping you mind your p's and q's?

parts.words: One helping you mind your p's and q's?
parts.note: minding your p's and q's normally means good manners; here it means saying the letters p and q properly, the work of someone treating a speech defect

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being polite is read literally as articulating letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinician who treats disorders of articulation and voice.

clue.text: Wavering Sinatra missing intro after heist in which son is picked up

indicators.note: after means the first piece comes before the second

indicators.text: in which son is picked up
indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted higher in the word, so the letter moves nearer the top

parts.note: taken as written before the letter moves

indicators.note: missing intro means the name loses its first letter

parts.note: Nancy Sinatra, singer and daughter of Frank

explanation.surface: Sinatra hesitates after a robbery in which her son is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinatra' points at Frank, but it is Nancy, minus N: ANCY. In HEIST the S is lifted to give HESIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecision, the state of holding back before acting.

clue.text: Shakes that come with plenty of sauce?

definitions.text: Shakes that come with plenty of sauce?

parts.words: Shakes that come with plenty of sauce?
parts.note: sauce is slang for alcohol, and the shakes are the trembling of a heavy drinker in withdrawal, not milkshakes served with a topping

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakes' and 'sauce' suggest a dessert menu; 'the sauce' is slang for strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin medical name for the tremors and hallucinations of alcohol withdrawal.

clue.text: Fruit tree Conservative current prime minister briefly pruned

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: briefly pruned means the name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Liz Truss was briefly a UK prime minister in 2022

explanation.surface: A Tory prime minister's short spell is likened to a pruned tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' also nods at Truss's famously short time in office.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon, orange and lime trees belong to this genus of fruiting trees.

clue.text: Feral beast lately seen roaming around Cape area

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the two abbreviations
roaming means wandering about, so the letters of lately move into a new order

parts.note: C is a standard abbreviation for Cape on maps

explanation.surface: A wild animal has recently been spotted wandering near the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roaming' turns LATELY into ALLEYT, and 'around' puts CA inside it before the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray town cat living wild on the streets and back lanes.

clue.text: Inexperienced boy carrying empty salsa dish

parts.note: green means inexperienced

indicators.note: empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving the first and last

parts.note: carrying in a down clue means the lower piece holds up the one above it

explanation.surface: A novice boy brings a bowl of salsa that has been eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold course of mixed leaves.

clue.text: Be responsible for mixing up "Peter" and "pater"

indicators.note: mixing up tells you to scramble the letters of the two quoted names together

explanation.surface: Someone confuses the names Peter and pater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing up' scrambles the ten letters of PETER and PATER together.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit a crime or blunder is to be the one who carries it out.

clue.text: A kid fed Jimmy peeled fruit

parts.note: per means a, as in once a day

indicators.note: fed means given something inside, so the peeled name goes into the word for kid

parts.note: a son is a kid

indicators.note: peeled removes the outer letters, leaving only the middle

explanation.surface: A child is fed some peeled fruit by Jimmy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' takes JIMMY down to IMM, which 'fed' puts inside SON.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange tomato-like fruit from an Asian tree.

clue.text: Stagger from Barking, heading westbound

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means travelling right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: barking means mad, as is nuts

explanation.surface: A traveller staggers out of Barking, a district of east London, heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is also an east London district, which is why the westbound journey fits the picture; here it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish them, to knock them senseless with surprise.

clue.text: Occupant of bed returned cover from plug

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
off can mean from, as in take it off the shelf
an ad, advert, is a plug

explanation.surface: Someone takes a cover off a plug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses LID OFF AD as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring flower grown in garden beds, so it lives in one.

clue.text: Wander round the Catholic church during annunciation

indicators.note: annunciation here means pronouncing, so the place name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Rome stands for the Roman Catholic Church by metonymy

explanation.surface: Someone wanders about a Catholic church during the feast of the Annunciation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annunciation' suggests the Feast of the Annunciation; here it just means saying aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to travel aimlessly about a place.

clue.text: Distinctly mimics retired traitor, see?

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to ape is to mimic
a rat is a betrayer
Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Someone impersonates a traitor who has gone into retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns APES into SEPA; a see is a bishop's diocese, and the Ely see is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart, individually, each on its own: the adverb of distinct parts.

clue.text: Sophisticated conclave ultimately supports Pope

indicators.note: in a down clue supports means sits underneath, so this letter comes after

parts.note: Urban is the name of several popes

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word conclave

explanation.surface: The conclave of cardinals ultimately backs a new pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave, polished and worldly in manner.

clue.text: Investment return from notes deposited in the current month

indicators.note: deposited in means placed inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is old business-letter style for this month
te and re are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Money is paid into an account this month to earn a return.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant, old commercial jargon for 'this month') holds TE and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Money earned on savings or a loan, the yield on capital.

clue.text: Runs away from British aerial bombardment terrified

indicators.note: away from means the first piece is taken out of the second

parts.note: an RAF raid is a bombing attack by the Royal Air Force
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: People flee a British air raid in terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs away' reads as fleeing; it is R taken out of RAF RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightened, scared stiff.

clue.text: Use towel after washing dirty puppy periodically

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone towels a dirty puppy dry after its wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe the dishes with a tea towel once they have been washed.

clue.text: Neighbour cycling, which is forbidden

indicators.note: cycling means a letter moves round from one end to the other

parts.note: to neighbour is to abut, to border on

explanation.surface: A neighbour cycles somewhere that is off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neighbour' is a verb: ABUT with its last letter moved to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of taboo, meaning prohibited.

clue.text: I'd claim shame, say, affected late bloomer

indicators.note: affected means altered or disturbed, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to a sense of shame that has affected them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' scrambles the fifteen letters of I'D CLAIM SHAME SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: This aster flowers around Michaelmas, the end of September, late in the gardening year.

clue.text: Relative temperature finally dropped in city on the Med

indicators.note: dropped in means placed within, so the letter goes inside the city

parts.note: Nice is a French city on the Mediterranean

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word temperature

explanation.surface: A relative's temperature dropped while staying in a Mediterranean city.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: Discarded clothing half unfastened in bed on board

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket long out of fashion

indicators.note: half means only the first two of the four letters are kept

parts.note: unfastened means open

explanation.surface: Someone half undressed lies in bed while aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: On a dartboard each scoring segment is called a bed; this one is the double-twenty ring at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts this is the double-twenty segment, a narrow scoring area on the dartboard.
